messages.author: 71171f0d61fc140f
messages.subject: Weird facet_grid() labeling bug
parts:
Hi all,

I think I've found a strange bug in labeling facets in facet_grid().
I'm writing up notes to demonstrate to a study group how to use
faceting and control scales. Here's the data I'm working with.

jean <- read.csv("http://www.ling.upenn.edu/~joseff/data/jean2.csv")
ay <- subset(jean, VClass %in% c("ay","ay0"))
ay$VClass <- as.factor(as.character(ay$VClass))

ay.m <- melt(ay, id = c("Time","RTime", "Word","VClass"), measure =
c("F1","F2"))

I'd like to facet by the Vowel Class and by the variable.

ggplot(ay.m, aes(Time, value, group = Word)) +
geom_line()+
facet_grid(VClass ~ variable)

Now, each level of the variable has a different scale, so it wouldn't
be totally inappropriate to plot the data with free y scales. However,
"free_y" doesn't appear to be possible if you facet vertically. That
makes good sense, so I tried this:

ggplot(ay.m, aes(Time, value, group = Word)) +
geom_line()+
facet_grid(VClass + variable~ ., scales = "free_y")

Now, the y scales are free, but the facets are labeled strangely. The
facet labels are [ay | ay], [ay0 | ay0], [F2 | F1], [F2 | F1]. Based
on the plotted data, the facet labels should be [ay | F1], [ay | F2],
[ay0 | F1] , [ay0 | F2].

-Joe
